subject.title: fix(mxc): reject oversized sandbox policy files

question: Should MXC reject all existing sandbox policy files over 1 MiB at startup, or should the bound be selected and documented through an explicit compatibility decision?
rationale: The hard limit deliberately changes the accepted plugin configuration surface for operators whose policy files were previously valid, and the review context does not establish that 1 MiB is an approved permanent contract.

options.title: Approve and document the 1 MiB contract
options.body: Keep the hard limit, describe the upgrade failure mode and remediation, and add validation for the chosen accepted-size boundary.

options.title: Choose a different compatibility boundary
options.body: Adopt a maintainer-approved limit or configuration strategy that protects startup memory while accommodating legitimate MXC policy sizes.

recommendation.title: Approve and document the 1 MiB contract
recommendation.body: Keep the hard limit, describe the upgrade failure mode and remediation, and add validation for the chosen accepted-size boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They can address the implementation details, while a current-main MXC owner should confirm the permanent configuration contract after a history pass.
